partnerships.name: Los Angeles County Department of Health Services
partnerships.description: The second-largest county health system in the U.S., DHS provides integrated care to over 670,000 residents annually through 19 health centers, 3 hospitals, and community clinics. It serves diverse populations, including justice-involved youth, older adults, and those in foster care. As part of the LA County Health Agency, DHS partners with USC and UCLA and is a major hub for postgraduate medical training.

partnerships.name: The Lundquist Institute for Biomedical Innovation
partnerships.description: Based at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center, the Lundquist Institute is a nonprofit research organization supporting clinical and translational research across many health areas. As the fiscal sponsor of the HIV Clinical Fellowship, it provides financial and administrative oversight, while DHS leads the clinical and educational programs.

partnerships.name: ViiV Healthcare
partnerships.description: ViiV Healthcare is a global HIV-focused company advancing treatment, prevention, and health equity. It provides financial support for the fellowship but does not influence curriculum, operations, or fellow selection, which are independently managed by DHS and academic partners.

coreCollaborators.name: USC Keck School of Medicine, Department of Family Medicine
coreCollaborators.description: A leader in patient-centered care and social justice, the USC Department of Family Medicine was home to one of the first AIDS Education and Training Centers (AETCs) in the U.S. It remains a key partner in workforce development and HIV primary care training.

coreCollaborators.name: Pacific AIDS Education and Training Center (PAETC)
coreCollaborators.description: Founded in 1988, PAETC builds provider capacity for high-quality HIV care, especially in underserved communities. Through multidisciplinary training for MDs, NPs, PAs, and pharmacists, it supports clinicians serving marginalized populations, including those who are unhoused or incarcerated. Its UCSF-based regional office coordinates eight local sites, over 300 Ryan White clinics, and 219 FQHCs at nearly 2,000 locations.

coreCollaborators.name: UCLA National Clinician Scholars Program (NCSP)
coreCollaborators.description: NCSP prepares early-career physicians and nurses for healthcare leadership, with a focus on disparities and quality of care. Fellows complete a customized six-month curriculum covering health policy, community-based research, and leadership.

coreCollaborators.name: Maternal Child Adolescent Center for Infectious Diseases and Virology (MCA)
coreCollaborators.description: Founded in 1988 during the pediatric HIV epidemic, MCA is California’s largest multidisciplinary Family HIV Center. Now part of LA General’s Rand Schrader Clinic, it provides culturally responsive care to women, children, youth, and families, and remains a vital fellowship training site for perinatal and family-based HIV care.

coreCollaborators.name: Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science & Drew CARES (CDU)
coreCollaborators.description: CDU, one of only four Historically Black Medical Colleges and a Hispanic-serving institution, is rooted in social justice and health equity. Its HIV-focused arm, Drew CARES, advances HIV prevention, treatment, research, and training through community partnerships and serves as a key clinical and educational site for fellows.

coreCollaborators.name: Center for HIV Identification, Prevention, and Treatment Services (CHIPTS)
coreCollaborators.description: A collaboration of UCLA, CDU, Friends Research Institute, and RAND, CHIPTS is funded by the National Institute of Mental Health. It supports research, innovation, and capacity building to reduce HIV disparities worldwide, providing fellows with research and policy mentorship.
